mesmaReviewEmTresPlataformas.text:
I loved this! The story follows a common historical romance manhwa trope, but the development and pacing were done so well. There were no dragging parts or unnecessary chapters, which made it such an enjoyable read. The FL was beautiful, courageous, and wise, though a little naive when it came to matters of the heart. The ML was such a green flag! He started off as a bit of a tsundere, but his character development throughout the story was really satisfying to watch.
The side characters, especially the kids, were absolutely adorable and lovable. They were honestly the main reason I started reading this in the first place. As for the antagonists, they were decent enough to make the story more interesting and keep the conflicts engaging.
And the art was absolutely gorgeous!!! Everyone looked so beautiful and handsome, and the outfits were stunning too. ✨
Overall, I would definitely recommend this to historical romance manhwa fans. You just need to tolerate the misunderstandings in the first part because after that, it becomes such a good read.👌🏼
PS. I DEMAND AN AFTER STORY FOR THE SECOND GENERATION! IT SHOULD BE ILLEGAL TO TEASE US WITH THAT AND NOT CONTINUE IT HUHU! 😭

versaoLongaEResumida.text:
I love love love this manwha!! Oh my goodness, I can't believe I stumbled upon something so good! This manwha discusses insecurities, trauma, and a whole array of topics that I was surprised to see, and what was the most surprising, was the fact they're shown in a very thorough way. Not to mention the story is very enjoyable. I am a very big fan of Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom and I highly recommend it!
Okay, I'll start off by talking about the story, because everything else I want to mention will go on for quite awhile. The story might seem like the standard, relatively happy stepmom romance manwha story, but it's not. It's a story of working through insecurities, trauma and prejudice. Abigail is reincarnated as the evil stepmother from snow white, but she wants to treat her daughter well, and that becomes her top priority. So she does, she truly tries to make her daughter happy, and she succeeds, becoming like a mother to her. And while she doesn't get along well with Sabrian originally, she tries to work on their relationship so that he can become a better father to Blanche. And after quite awhile and lots of work, they become a family, truly caring about each other. I really liked seeing the family slowly bond. However, the way they bond is more on the complicated side, which I'll talk more about now.
Starting off with Abigail who I think was very well-written, and in a sense that I was surprised. Abigail was over-weight in her past life, and therefore struggled with prejudice against her. She was outcasted and treated badly, thus feeling lesser than others. She experienced quite a difficult life, but even through it all, she continued working and moving on. Though she had to face many insecurities. So when she reincarnates as Abigail, she doesn't want to go through what she previously went through. As she creates bonds between the family, she begins to grow happier and eat more, thus worrying about her weight. She begins to starve herself and think she wasn't worthy of love because of her weight. However, she's soon shown that this isn't true in the slightest, because Sabrian and Blanche truly love her, they don't care about her weight. She defies norms and lives according to what makes her happy, not letting the mean comments from others get to her. Abigail learns that she should live true to herself.
Next is Sabrian, who started out as a complete jerk, but is now one of my favorite male leads. Originally, he acts as if he despises Abigail. But this isn't just because he's some cold black-haired, stereotypical emperor. This is because of the trauma he's faced in the past with women. He's afraid of contact with them and the manwha really shows how much this affects him and how what he went through truly impacts him. Sabrian begins to grow feelings for Abigail though, and he wants to show his feelings, so despite being afraid to touch women, he slowly works towards becoming more comfortable with Abigail. Going from holding hands briefly to hugging each other. His trauma doesn't go away, but he works through it and doesn't let it stop him.
Blanche was growing up with a father and mother who didn't show her love. Yet now that Abigail changed due to the reincarnation, she's being shown love. However, Blanche has always grown up to try and be perfect. She's rather proper and doesn't act like a child at all. She holds back eating, wears corsets, and does many things that are considered unhealthy for a child. Yet as she's shown more love, she realizes this isn't necessary, and like Abigail, she should live happily and enjoy her childhood.
Vertius is trapped inside a mirror and he feels lonely. Yet despite this, he begins to find family in Blanche, Abigail and Sabrian. He yearns to be with them and it's sad yet he's so sweet. He's also really funny. I really like his relationship with Blanche and I look forward to seeing what happens to him.
This manwha really surprised me with how much it goes against what I usually see in other fantasy romance manwhas. It talks about fatphobia and really works through insecurities. It also doesn't negatively depict LGBTQ-related stuff. Along with all that, it shows that women should live according to what makes them happy and not act a certain way because of other people. Abigail shows this a lot. The words she receives from others hurt her, but she doesn't let their words stop her. The manwha shows that you should be kind to all, to not judge and to live true to yourself.
I really like the family aspect in this manwha. It takes awhile for them to really begin bonding, but going slow really did the manwha good because it let the story explore what their characters were going through and how becoming closer as a family impacted each character. So in the end, now that they're like a family, it seems like they genuinely care each other and it wasn't just rushed for the sake of the story.
I certainly recommend reading this manwha. It really surpised me. I'm really enjoying it and all the main characters. I can't wait for the fourth season!

opinioesParecidasIndependentes.text:
Fast-paced, wholesome, and easy to read—this story has great character relationships and no unnecessary drama. The FL is smart, the ML is supportive, and their chemistry feels natural. Overall, it’s a light and satisfying read with a happy ending.
The story doesn’t drag unnecessarily, which makes it easy and fun to read. There are no frustrating misunderstandings and no love triangle. The communication between the characters is clear and healthy, especially between the FL and ML.
All the characters are likable, and I especially loved the FL’s warm family dynamic. The FL is smart and capable, and the ML is a green flag. Their relationship feels natural.
Even the villain is simple—not overly smart or dumb—but still interesting enough to keep you engaged.
The story uses common tropes, but it is still enjoyable. The art is nice, and the emotions are drawn well—even when the FL is in squirrel form.
It has a happy and clean ending, which makes it satisfying overall. If you want something light and enjoyable, this is definitely worth reading.

comentarioCurtoEReviewLonga.text: The story is confusing, but it's okay if you turn your brain off and just enjoy the smut.

This seems to be part of a series called 속박의 고리 Chains of Restraint/Rings of Bondage which consists of 3 books by the same author Na Seop 나섭

'Imprint 각인' & 'Imprisonment 감금' are adapted into manhwas while I'm not sure if there is any plan for the last one 'contract 계약'.

For this one, I'd say the Art and SMUT are decent but with only 3 chapters out. I find the plot is a bit confusing lol I didn't really know what I was reading hahaha So better to just enjoy the SMUT and turn off your brain

And The Imprint one is just out today. It's basically a SMUT take on a teenage boy(who came of age at the start of the story btw) crush on his teacher trope but in a Omegaverse with Historical manhwa setting

reviewDivididaEmDuasPostagens.text: [MINOR SPOILERS] I wanted to give this manhwa a higher rating it had so much potential. The original premise was so interesting but i feel like a lot of it got ignored and the story started neglecting plot holes. It had such a strong beginning and if it remained faithful to that storyline it could've been an amazing manhwa. I really like the idea of her being his salvation, but the way the story is paced leaves little room for development and it's quite confusing.

@chureito Like what happened to the pocket watch, hell, the curse???? So many important things were either brushed over or never mentioned again. It's a shame because I really would've liked it a lot more if it wasn't so focused on political drama and more on the two characters. I feel like they have concepts of a great story but the execution was poorly done. I so badly wanted to like this more, I kept sticking out for hope.
